newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Evergreen winds down west coast peak service.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen winds down west coast peak service.

text.p: Evergreen International Airlines Inc has ended its temporary peak season weekly flight from Hong Kong to Los Angeles, vice president Kersti Krepp told Reuters.
But demand for Evergreen's five remaining Boeing 747 flights a week from Hong Kong to Columbus, Ohio and New York remains high, she said.
"All flights have been full and we could have easily sold two airplanes for every one we have sold," Krepp said in an interview from her Hong Kong office.

"Yields have not been where they need to be but from a demand side the market has significantly improved over the last couple of years. The market was strong even in June this year which is not usually a good month," she added.

"Some carriers have taken capacity out of the market and the supply side has not exceeded demand. There is definitely fewer aircraft this year and even early into December some operators are reducing the amount of capacity when aircraft go to serve the domestic US market," she added.
Evergreen's U.S. east coast schedule is due to be reduced to four flights per week when the Monday service is discontinued after December 23, she added.
